# Modes of inquiry: definitions, evidence, and the graph {.unnumbered}

[Drafted]{.status .drafted} [the next meeting · graph v0.4 drafted · literature read October 16 to 19, 2026 · not yet discussed]{.status-line}

- The next meeting. It defines the thirteen [mode profiles](glossary.qmd#working-mode-specifications) from the literature, places them on the [unit graph](unit.qmd#the-graph), and asks what the evidence says about modes and novelty, breadth, and advance.
- Each mode will become an agent. This page is the evidence the agents' rubrics start from; the [mode pages](glossary.qmd#working-mode-specifications) carry the rubric itself.
- **Slides for the meeting:** [open the deck](slides/modes-meeting.html) (arrow keys to move, F for full screen).
- **Eight papers walked through the graph:** [Walking the graph](walks.qmd).

## The meeting

| | |
|:--|:--|
| Central question | Which kinds of scientific work does an agent family need, where was each defined, and has any been shown to raise novelty, breadth, or advance? |
| Anchor | @elliott2016, full text, open access. Read "A richer account of scientific practice" and their Figure 3. |
| Companion | @betts2021, open access. The rotating reader presents the coding scheme and Figure 4. |
| Geoscience pair, optional | @pfister2017 and @baker2017, the *Water Resources Research* debate on hypothesis testing in hydrology. |
| Bring | One paper of your own, with its modes named in order from the table in section 2. |
| Output | A decision on the mode list (keep, split, merge, add), each with the source that forces it; graph v0.4 adopted, amended, or rejected; one [ledger](notes.qmd#inquiry-mode-ledger) row. |

- Why these two: Elliott and colleagues name plural modes and judge research by "the alignment between the nature of the knowledge gap or challenge addressed and the combination of approaches or methods used" [@elliott2016]. Betts and colleagues coded 268 ecology and evolution papers, found multiple alternative hypotheses in 6.7% and no citation or grant advantage for any hypothesis use, and still argue for more of it [@betts2021].
- One conceptual, one empirical, and they disagree: Elliott judges by fit to the knowledge gap, Betts by the clarity that rival hypotheses bring. Neither is geoscience; the optional pair is.

## 1. What a mode is

- **Working definition.** A mode of inquiry is a kind of epistemic work, named by the gain it aims at and the evidence its claims owe. It describes an episode or an action, not a whole paper.
- **Precedent for the word.** O'Malley, Elliott, and Burian name four modes of research practice: hypothesis-driven, exploratory, question-driven, and technology-oriented [@omalley2010, as reported in @elliott2012]. Moving back and forth between them is "methodological iteration" [@elliott2012].
- **Not the same as:**

| Term | Unit | Source | Relation to our modes |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Style of reasoning | A long-lived tradition: six in Crombie, plus a laboratory and an "algorismic" style in Hacking | @crombie1988; @hacking2002 | Coarser; one style holds several modes |
| Epistemic culture | A field's machinery for making knowledge | @knorr1999 | Orthogonal; a culture uses many modes |
| Paradigm, in Gray's sense | An era: empirical, theoretical, computational, data-intensive | @hey2009 | A period label; the fourth spans three of our modes |
| Mode 1 / Mode 2 | How knowledge production is organized | [glossary](glossary.qmd#purpose-and-use) | Term collision only |
| Method, in this book | A composition of units on the graph | [unit, section 6](unit.qmd#composing-units-into-a-mode) | How a mode runs the graph |
| Contribution type | What a paper delivers: data, estimate, method, concept | [glossary](glossary.qmd#coding-an-episode) | The output, not the work |

- **How modes relate, four claims in the literature:**
  - Historical sequence, cumulative: Crombie's order of emergence; Gray's four paradigms [@crombie1988; @hey2009].
  - Coexistence with unequal stability: "The taxonomic and the historic-genetic styles have produced nothing like the stability of the laboratory or the mathematical style" [@hacking2002].
  - Iteration: data- and technology-driven programmes are "complementary and iterative partners" of hypothesis-led work [@kell2004, p. 99; @elliott2012; @elliott2016].
  - Institutional hierarchy: some funders privilege hypothesis testing [@omalley2009, pp. 612–613; @haufe2013], as do US courts judging scientific testimony [@haufe2013, p. 364]; school science teaches the single-variable experiment [@manduca2012, p. 2]. Haufe's reason: hypothesis testing is the easiest to appraise, not the best (p. 366).
- The book adopts iteration. The hierarchy is a claim about practice, and section 5 tests it.

## 2. Thirteen definitions and where they come from

| Mode | Gain it aims at | Defined as distinct work by | Contested boundary |
|:-------|:------|:---------|:------|
| **[Question-driven inquiry](modes/question.qmd)** | A question framed so that some result would answer it, and reframed when a pass ends without a conclusion | Named only by @omalley2009 and @omalley2010, with @elliott2012; parts of a question from @vanfraassen1980 and @nickles1981 | No evidence standard in the mode literature; the seminar assembles one |
| **[Observation and description](modes/observation.qmd)** | A credible record of a phenomenon, its variability, and what is unobserved | Data versus phenomena [@bogen1988]; "'Descriptive' in science is a pejorative, almost always preceded by 'merely'" [@grimaldi2007] | No peer-reviewed account gives description its own success criteria |
| **[Exploratory inquiry](modes/exploration.qmd)** | Phenomena, questions, and representations | Experimentation "not ... driven by specific theories" [@steinle1997, p. S65]; "mapping activities" [@franklin2005, p. 893]; extended to observational data [@pietsch2015, p. 914] | Steinle's exploration aims at regularities, so it overlaps the last row |
| **[Hypothesis assessment](modes/hypothesis.qmd)** | Discrimination among rivals | "He invents hypotheses and he invents tests for them" [@gilbert1896, p. 2]; the smoking gun [@cleland2002, p. 480] | Generation and test are separate actions, already in Gilbert |
| **[Theory and mechanistic modeling](modes/theory.qmd)** | Concepts, explanations, valid derivations | Models as mediating instruments [@morrison1999]; modeling is "indirect representation and analysis" [@weisberg2007, p. 207] | Weisberg separates modeling from other theorizing; our row joins them |
| **[Simulation and prediction](modes/simulation.qmd)** | Computed consequences; assessed forecasts | "A new kind of scientific method" [@humphreys2004]; @winsberg2010; prediction as a goal [@shmueli2010] | Computer simulation studies are "material experiments in a straightforward sense," though simulations as such are not [@parker2009, pp. 483, 495]; the row joins a method with a goal |
| **[Instruments and observing systems](modes/instruments.qmd)** | A reliable new measurement capability | Experimentation "has a life of its own" [@hacking1983, p. 150]; instruments "express knowledge" [@baird2004]; @rheinberger2011 | Merged with methods as "technology-oriented" [@omalley2009, p. 612; @omalley2010] |
| **[Methods and computation](modes/methods.qmd)** | A new inference or computational capability | No source defines it as a mode. Nearest: the algorismic style "dedicated to finding algorithms" [@hacking2002]; tools that become theories [@gigerenzer1991] | Gap |
| **[Cross-study synthesis](modes/synthesis.qmd)** | A pooled estimate or a connection across studies that no single study supports | Meta-analysis [@gurevitch2018]; synthesis centres [@carpenter2009] | Where pooling ends and a new estimate begins |
| **[Reconstruction from traces](modes/reconstruction.qmd)** | A constrained history of a past event, retained against stated rival histories | Historical science [@cleland2002]; prehistory from traces [@turner2007] | Whether convergent traces confirm or only explain |
| **[Replication and robustness](modes/robustness.qmd)** | What survives repetition, perturbation, transfer | Replication: @schmidt2009replication; @machery2020. Robustness: @wimsatt2012; @parker2011 | Defined for experiments and model ensembles. Nearest for a one-off natural event: conceptual replication, a test of the hypothesis "with different methods" [@schmidt2009replication, p. 91] |
| **[Inferential estimation](modes/estimation.qmd)** | A latent quantity with uncertainty and resolution | @backus1968 (resolution); @tarantola2005 (uncertainty); inversion in philosophy: @bokulich2017 | Absent from every general taxonomy |
| **[Statistical modeling and empirical regularities](modes/regularities.qmd)** | A relation or distribution with a warranted range | Crombie's style (e) [@hacking2002]; two cultures [@breiman2001]; descriptive versus explanatory models [@shmueli2010] | Overlaps exploration |

: {tbl-colwidths="[24,20,32,24]"}

- **Three modes have no source that defines them as a distinct mode:** methods and computation, inferential estimation, and replication for non-repeatable natural events, where conceptual replication is the nearest [@schmidt2009replication, p. 91]. Estimation is where geophysics wrote its own founding texts [@backus1968; @tarantola2005]; its only philosophical treatment is @bokulich2017.
- **Missing relative to the precedents:** question-driven inquiry [@omalley2010] and systematic invention, or engineering design [@pickstone2007]. The book keeps question origin as a ledger attribute (decided September 10, 2026). O'Malley and colleagues are the case against that decision.
- **Proposed for the room: split synthesis.** Research synthesis across studies and reconstruction from traces owe different evidence (study selection versus common-cause inference), and no precedent joins them. One agent system was 85.5% accurate on its data-analysis statements and 57.9% on its synthesis statements [@mitchener2025, preprint].
- **Geoscience accounts agree on three points:** explanatory pluralism, narrative with causal explanation [@kleinhans2005]; several rivals at once [@gilbert1896; @cleland2002]; model-laden data [@bokulich2017; @bokulich2020]. They differ on how far laboratory accounts fit: geoscience tests hypotheses, but against observations and through "multiple converging lines of evidence" rather than single-variable experiments [@manduca2012, pp. 1–2], or field work does not fit a philosophy built on the laboratory [@raab2002; @baker2017].

## 3. The modes on the graph (v0.4, drafted)

- Graph v0.3 draws one hypothesis pass. In 13 of the 18 geoscience advances in section 4, the first decisive move was an observation, an instrument, or a method, made before any rival existed. v0.3 can place those only as entry states.
- v0.4 adds three nodes, each forced by a source, drawn dashed until the group adopts them. The figure and the log are on [the unit page](unit.qmd#the-graph).

| Node | Move | Forced by |
|:--|:--|:--|
| E. Explore: establish the phenomenon | From data to a phenomenon: does it repeat; is it in the measurement chain or in the world | @bogen1988; @steinle1997; the v0.3 surprise edge [@klahr1999, p. 537] |
| N. New capability: build and characterize an instrument or method | A capability claim, made before any theory | @hacking1983, pp. 160, 163; Lehmann on the missing vertical-component records [@kolblebert2001, p. 264]; @keeling1960 |
| I. Estimate a latent quantity | Invert observations through a forward model; state resolution and uncertainty | @backus1968 (resolution); @tarantola2005 (uncertainty); data are model-laden [@bokulich2020] |

- Node labels use the words of the mode taxonomy; [the crosswalk](unit.qmd#the-graph) on the unit page maps each node to the modes it serves.
- Two compositions are added: **capability first** (N, O, E, then Q), forced by Lehmann and Keeling; **forecast verification** (the expectation frozen at S before O exists, C at a later date), forced by @charney1950 (p. 245: "we were just able to keep pace with the weather").
- Each mode as a path on the graph:

| Mode | Usual entry | Nodes it runs | What it retains, and where |
|:-------|:----|:----|:----------|
| Question-driven inquiry | Problem, no conclusion | Q, then the start of the tree | A reframed question with its diagnosis (Q) |
| Observation | Capability, data | N, O, E | A phenomenon or a coverage limit (E) |
| Exploration | Anomaly, data without theory | E and O in a loop; Q reframed | A candidate phenomenon or a new question (E, Q) |
| Hypothesis assessment | Problem, prediction | Q through R | A retained or excluded rival (K, X) |
| Theory and modeling | Problem, anomaly | H, S | A concept or a valid derivation (S); empirical adequacy later, at K |
| Simulation and prediction | Prediction | S by computation; O later; C | An assessed forecast (C) |
| Instruments | Capability | N, O | A characterized measurement chain (N) |
| Methods and computation | Capability | N, I | An inference procedure with known failure cases (N, I) |
| Cross-study synthesis | Problem | O over many studies; C; K | A pooled estimate with its spread (K) |
| Reconstruction from traces | Anomaly, problem | H; F found; O over independent traces; K | A best explanation within a stated rival set (K) |
| Replication and robustness | A challenged result | V, or the whole unit rerun | A corrected or supported range (V, X, K) |
| Estimation | Data | O, I | A latent quantity with resolution (I) |
| Regularities | Data without theory | E, K | A relation with a stated range (K) |

: {tbl-colwidths="[26,20,18,36]"}

- Each mode is defined here by what it writes into Cleland's schema, $H + A + C \Rightarrow E$: the rivals $H$, the auxiliaries $A$ (instrument theory, forward model, processing), the conditions $C$, the expectations $E$, and the observations $O$ they are compared with. The figure is the bridge between the definitions and the [decision tree](decision-tree.qmd), which calls the modes in turn until the schema is complete enough for a claim.

::: {#fig-mode-map .column-body-outset}

```{=html}
<div class="schema">
<div class="sc-row"><div class="sc-term"><div class="sc-sym">Q</div><div class="sc-name">question</div><ul><li><a href="modes/question.qmd"><b>Question-driven inquiry</b></a> frames and reframes it</li><li><a href="modes/exploration.qmd"><b>Exploration</b></a> turns a phenomenon into one</li></ul></div><div class="sc-op">→</div><div class="sc-term "><div class="sc-sym">H</div><div class="sc-name">rival hypotheses</div><ul><li><a href="modes/theory.qmd"><b>Theory</b></a> proposes a mechanism</li><li><a href="modes/hypothesis.qmd"><b>Hypothesis assessment</b></a> keeps a set of rivals</li><li><a href="modes/regularities.qmd"><b>Regularities</b></a> a relation proposed as a law</li></ul></div><div class="sc-op">+</div><div class="sc-term "><div class="sc-sym">A</div><div class="sc-name">auxiliaries</div><ul><li><a href="modes/instruments.qmd"><b>Instruments</b></a> theory of the instrument</li><li><a href="modes/methods.qmd"><b>Methods</b></a> the processing and inference</li><li><a href="modes/theory.qmd"><b>Theory</b></a> background laws, forward model</li></ul></div><div class="sc-op">+</div><div class="sc-term "><div class="sc-sym">C</div><div class="sc-name">conditions</div><ul><li><a href="modes/hypothesis.qmd"><b>Hypothesis assessment</b></a> set by the investigator</li><li><a href="modes/reconstruction.qmd"><b>Reconstruction</b></a> found: one past event</li><li><a href="modes/regularities.qmd"><b>Regularities</b></a> found: nature repeats it</li></ul></div><div class="sc-op">⇒</div><div class="sc-term "><div class="sc-sym">E</div><div class="sc-name">expectations</div><ul><li><a href="modes/theory.qmd"><b>Theory</b></a> derived by hand</li><li><a href="modes/simulation.qmd"><b>Simulation</b></a> computed</li></ul></div></div>
<div class="sc-cmp"><span>compared with</span></div>
<div class="sc-row sc-row2"><div class="sc-term sc-obs"><div class="sc-sym">O</div><div class="sc-name">observations</div><ul><li><a href="modes/observation.qmd"><b>Observation</b></a> a record with provenance</li><li><a href="modes/exploration.qmd"><b>Exploration</b></a> a phenomenon that repeats</li><li><a href="modes/instruments.qmd"><b>Instruments</b></a> a new capability to observe</li><li><a href="modes/reconstruction.qmd"><b>Reconstruction</b></a> independent traces</li><li><a href="modes/synthesis.qmd"><b>Cross-study synthesis</b></a> pooled results across studies</li><li><a href="modes/estimation.qmd"><b>Estimation</b></a> O*: a latent quantity inferred from O</li></ul></div><div class="sc-op">→</div><div class="sc-term sc-check"><div class="sc-sym">V</div><div class="sc-name">replication and robustness</div><ul><li><a href="modes/robustness.qmd"><b>Robustness</b></a> varies A and C; independent data, methods, models</li></ul></div><div class="sc-op">→</div><div class="sc-term sc-verdict"><div class="sc-name">verdict</div><ul><li>keep · exclude · contradict · no conclusion</li><li>protect: a logged move at question 7</li></ul></div></div>
</div>
```

What each mode writes into Cleland's schema (drafted). Top: the question $Q$ comes first; the hypothesis $H$, auxiliaries $A$, and conditions $C$ jointly imply the expectation $E$ [@cleland2001, pp. 987--988]. Bottom: the observations $E$ is compared with, the robustness check, and the verdict. Under each term, the modes that write it; a mode that writes two terms appears twice.
:::

## 4. How the modes have been studied

| Kind of evidence | What it can show | Examples | What it cannot show |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Philosophy and history | Definitions; what warrant each mode owes | Section 2 | Prevalence; effect on outcomes |
| Cognitive and ethnographic studies | How scientists move between modes | @klahr1988; @fugelsang2004; @macleod2016 | Outcomes at scale |
| Science of science | Associations between contribution type and citation, disruption, prizes | Section 5 | Causation; advance |
| Documented episodes | Which modes did the decisive work, in what order | The table below | Base rates; failures are missing |

| The martian core (2021) | Capability | Instruments, observation, estimation | @stahler2021 |
| Machine-learned medium-range weather forecasts (2023) | Capability: reanalysis and compute | Method, simulation and prediction, robustness (1,380 verification targets) | @lam2023 |

| Count over these 10 | Episodes |
|:--|:--|
| First decisive mode was observation, an instrument, or a method | 6 |
| First decisive mode was synthesis | 2 |
| First decisive mode was theory | 1 |
| First decisive mode was robustness | 1 |
| A new instrument, archive, or computer was a precondition | 8, and 1 partial |
| An explicit hypothesis test did decisive work | 2, and 1 partial |

- Capability first still holds for most episodes (6 of 10, against 13 of 18 before 2010), but synthesis and robustness each led twice, which the earlier table never shows. This is a choice of episodes, not a trend.
- The one theory-first episode waited for an instrument: prompt gravity signals were predicted, then detected in superconducting-gravimeter and broadband records of Tohoku-Oki [@montagner2016; @vallee2017].
- Alternates not in the table: displacement reaching the Japan trench [@fujiwara2011]; global atmospheric waves from the Hunga eruption [@matoza2022].
- Ten advances chosen by impact and interdisciplinary uptake, several of them in the tables above, are candidates for the group's [success set](success-set.qmd), the positive test cases for scoring rules and agents, coded by mode from full text.
- Two of the four hypothesis-first episodes waited years or decades for a capability or a field programme (the ice ages; Cascadia).
- Acceptance times a source states: drift to plate tectonics, about fifty years [@oreskes1999]; the inner core, about twenty years [@kolblebert2001, p. 267]; Milankovitch to the pacemaker, about thirty-five years [@weart2008].
- Robustness in these episodes came from independent traces converging on one event, not from repeated experiments [@cleland2002]; for climate models, agreement across models confirms when read as variety of evidence [@lloyd2010].
- No study counts hypothesis-driven against descriptive papers in an Earth-science journal. Nearest: in ecology, 21 of 100 papers tested more than one hypothesis and 3 were purely descriptive [@betini2017]; in hydrology, hypothesis testing "rarely" matches the ideal (@pfister2017, abstract).

## 5. Do modes drive novelty, breadth, or advance?

- **Verdict.** No mode has been shown to cause novelty, breadth, or advance. Five contribution types have associations with citation or disruption, all outside the Earth sciences. Two quasi-experiments touch modes indirectly.

| Outcome | Strongest evidence | Modes involved | Kind | Status |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Novelty, disruption | New methods more disruptive, new theories less [@leahey2023]; an originality index tracks self-assessed theoretical, not methodological, originality in 246 life scientists [@shibayama2020] | Methods, theory | Association; the two metrics see different contribution types | Not established |
| Breadth | A cost shock to one sensing tool let generalists recruit specialists and widen the knowledge combined [@teodoridis2018]; methods and model templates cross fields [@gao2024; @knuuttila2023] | Instruments, methods, theory as template | One natural experiment; case studies | Carriers identified; payoff of breadth in modes unmeasured |
| Advance | Capability first in 13 of 18 episodes; hypothesis assessment decisive in 7, usually late | Instruments, methods, observation; hypothesis late | Coded episodes, not a sample | A hypothesis for the corpus study |
| Citation impact | Methods and synthesis cited most; hypothesis use null; failed replications cited more | See next table | Associations | Consistent outside geoscience |

| Mode | Novelty or disruption | Citation impact | Breadth |
|:-----|:------|:---------|:------|
| Observation | Not measured | Three ocean data sets out-cite 99% of oceanography articles [@belter2014]; case reports least cited in medicine [@patsopoulos2005] | Not measured |
| Exploration | Exploration-tolerant funding: lower keyword overlap with past work [@azoulay2011] | Fatter tails: +97% top-1% papers and +35% flops, 73 against 393 investigators [@azoulay2011]; risky strategies are 14.2% of statements and their extra reward does not cover the risk [@foster2015] | Not measured |
| Hypothesis assessment | Not measured | No advantage: β = −0.024, p = 0.83, N = 268 [@betts2021] | Not measured |
| Theory | New theories less disruptive [@leahey2023] | 28% fewer citations per main-text equation per page, lost among empirical citers; appendix equations had no effect (649 ecology and evolution papers, 1998) [@fawcett2012] | Templates travel; across disciplines their warrant may stay home [@knuuttila2016; @knuuttila2023] |
| Simulation | Not measured | Not measured | Computational templates reorganize fields [@humphreys2004] |
| Instruments | Prize counts disagree by coding: 82% "method" [@greenwald2012] against 77% discoveries in physics, 1901–2004, where 11 of 17 invention prizes were measuring instruments [@bartneck2008, pp. 74–75] | Not measured directly | Cheaper tools widen teams [@teodoridis2018] |
| Methods | New methods more disruptive [@leahey2023] | Bioinformatics tools are 34% of each year's top-20 most-cited papers [@wren2016] | AI methods rose from 0.5% to 1.3% of papers, 2000–2019 [@gao2024] |
| Synthesis | Not measured | Meta-analyses the most-cited design in health sciences [@patsopoulos2005]; reviews 2.95 times articles, mean of the 35 largest SCI-E categories, none in geoscience [@miranda2018]; synthesis-centre papers 82.7 against 42.9 citations [@hackett2021] | Topical diversity negatively related to citations [@hackett2021] |
| Replication | Not measured | Nonreplicable papers cited more [@serragarcia2021]; a failed replication cut citations about 9%, not significant [@vonhippel2022] | Not measured |
| Estimation | Not measured | Not measured | Not measured |
| Regularities | Not measured | Not measured | Not measured |

: {tbl-colwidths="[18,24,34,24]"}

- Read from abstracts only: @leahey2023, @wren2016. @miranda2018, @patsopoulos2005, @fawcett2012, and @bartneck2008 were checked against the full text on October 20, 2026. The rest were read in full or in an open preprint; the private analysis lists the basis per source.
- **Correctness and citation pull apart.** Citations do not reflect soundness or originality [@aksnes2019]; the replication rows show it directly.
- **Breadth is measured in topics and references, not modes.** A pivot away from one's own past references cuts the top-5% hit rate from 7.4% to 2.2% [@hill2025]; publishing into a distant audience makes a hit 3.5 times as likely [@shi2023]; generalists or specialists win depending on the field's pace [@teodoridis2019]. A hypothesis neither paper tests: carrying a home method to a distant audience is an expedition, not a pivot.
- **What travels and what stays.** Methods, instruments, and model templates cross fields; validation standards and task routines stay behind [@macleod2018].
- **One person, two modes.** Bimodal modeler-experimenters reported losing time switching, and their field doubted it could become the norm [@macleod2016, p. 409].
- **Teams of different approaches.** Diversity helps on rugged problems and costs speed; on smooth problems the best performers win [@hong2004; @grim2019, p. 108; @thoma2015; @wu2023]. The gain in Weisberg and Muldoon's model is the mavericks' own work [@weisberg2009; @alexander2015, p. 440].

**Claims this evidence does not support.**

- That hypothesis-driven papers have more impact [@betts2021].
- That most breakthroughs follow hypothesis testing: 81% of 761 major discoveries used it, with no comparison set [@krauss2024].
- That science is driven more by tools than ideas: the counts flip with the coding [@greenwald2012; @bartneck2008].
- That being cited means being correct [@serragarcia2021; @aksnes2019].
- That breadth in modes raises impact: no study measures it.
- That any of this holds in the Earth sciences: no impact study above uses an Earth-science corpus.

## 6. From modes to agents

- **No taxonomy of AI in science is organized by mode.** Surveys sort by workflow stage, autonomy, or mechanism [@zheng2025; @reddy2025]; one sorts by kind of understanding [@krenn2022]. The nearest to a mode list is the five geoscience problem classes of @karpatne2019.
- **Coverage.** Coded by this search over 19 published systems and benchmarks: the core loop runs methods in 7, hypothesis generation and ranking in 6, regularities in 4, literature synthesis in 4, and simulation, instruments, or replication in none. All 19 start from a supplied goal; none starts from an anomaly or reconstructs an event from physical traces.
- **Roles.** One multi-agent system splits agents by epistemic function: generation, reflection, ranking, evolution [@gottweis2026]. Others split by disciplinary persona, career rank, or tool [@swanson2025; @su2025; @schmidgall2025; @ghareeb2026].
- **Drift.** AI-augmented papers concentrate where data are abundant, topics shrink by 4.63%, and follow-on engagement falls by 22%; the authors read it as a move from questions of origin to operational ones, which they did not measure by mode [@hao2026]. Against it, LLM adopters cite 11.9% more books [@kusumegi2025].

| Design hypothesis | Evidence for | What would refute it |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Specialize agents by the evidence a mode owes, not by persona or by Peirce's labels | Search access for the reflection agent cut implausible hypotheses [@gottweis2026]; agents split by abduction, deduction, and induction were tested only on logic puzzles [@abdaljalil2025] | A generalist with the same tools and budget runs as many mode-specific checks as the specialists |
| Each mode agent has an evaluator the generating model does not control | Automated reviewers scored 6.1 of 10 against 3.8 from humans [@schmidgall2025]; the A-Lab scored itself [@leeman2024] | Self-scores track blinded expert scores |
| Synthesis is its own agent, scored apart from the analyses it draws on | 57.9% against 85.5% accuracy [@mitchener2025] | Synthesis accuracy equals analysis accuracy once scored separately |
| A system without a mode budget drifts to data-rich modes | @hao2026; the coverage counts above | Logged mode shares in the group's runs match the ledger without a budget |
| A method carried to a new field must carry that field's validation standard | @macleod2018; the Ising model lost its renormalization-group warrant moving from physics to socio-economics [@knuuttila2016] | Transferred methods pass the destination's checks without being given them |
| Specialists built on one base model are not a diverse team | Diversity's advantage depends on solvers that differ [@hong2004; @grim2019] | Same-model specialists generate as many distinct rivals as specialists on different models |
| The exploration agent enters from an anomaly | None of the 19 systems does; Kosmos "can sometimes veer in unexpected trajectories" [@mitchener2025, p. 19] | An agent given a goal finds the anomalies an anomaly-entry agent finds |

- **The polymath hypothesis, restated for agents.** A human's cost of holding two modes is training and switching time [@macleod2016]; an agent's switching cost is near zero. That is where a generalist could beat people. Test: one generalist agent against a team of three mode specialists on a task that needs simulation and observation, scored by a blinded specialist in each mode, recording whether each mode's own checks ran.

## 7. For the room

1. Decided by the convenor (October 21, 2026): synthesis split, question-driven inquiry added. For the room: does any other mode need splitting?
2. Is methods and computation a mode or a contribution type? Hacking gives it a style; no one gives it its own warrant.
3. Graph v0.4: do E, N, and I place your own paper better than v0.3 did?
4. Which outcome should a mode agent be scored on, by whom, and against what baseline?

- **Exercise.** Code your paper by mode, draw it as a path on the [decision tree](decision-tree.qmd), and mark the node where its decisive move happened. Then do the same for one row of the episode table and compare.
- **Record.** Sign the [notes](notes.qmd); one [ledger](notes.qmd#inquiry-mode-ledger) row; the decision on the list and on graph v0.4, with the source behind each change.

## What this page does not establish

- That any mode causes novelty, breadth, or advance.
- Base rates: the twenty-eight episodes are a selected set, coded by this search; four rows rest on a historian's coding, and the ten after 2010 rest on abstracts.
- That the agent hypotheses hold: none has been run on the group's agents.
